prior_year_events.impact_description: Large reduction in gross claims outstanding due to RITC transfer

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2019 were GBP 965.311m. Using the published gross claims development table, excluding the two most recent underwriting years, prior-year re-estimation produced a net adverse movement of approximately GBP 8.36m (strengthening), driven by adverse development in the 2017 underwriting year more than offsetting a release on the 2016 year. The claims development is presented gross and the 2018 effect of a significant RITC transfer materially affected prior-year balances and may distort comparability.
raw_causal_phrases: Unforeseen loss trends resulting from court rulings, changes in the law, differences in loss adjustment practice, medical and long-term care, and economic factors such as inflation can have a considerable impact on run-off results.
Large claims matters are reviewed during claims meetings.

As an example of this approach, an assessment of terrorism risk is based on a mixture of qualitative and quantitative data (e.g. for estimating property damage, business interruption, mortality and morbidity subsequent to an attack of a predefined magnitude), which is used to control, limit and manage aggregate terrorism exposure.
Included within reinsurance loss recoverable as at 31 December 2019 were amounts of GBP 33.8m (2018: GBP 33.0m) recoverable from a group company.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was calculated from the gross claims development table (cumulative gross claims incurred) on page 28 by excluding the two most recent underwriting years (2018 and 2019) and summing diagonal changes for 2016 and 2017. There is no single explicit textual sentence stating a gross prior-year movement. The 2018 'Effect of RITC' (gross -819.917k) is material and may distort comparability; the RITC is noted in the technical provisions reconciliation. exact_reserve_text not found.
